corrected_value.authors: Roberts, S. C., Little, A. C., Burriss, R. P., Cobey, K. D., Klapilová, K., Havlíček, J., et al.
corrected_value.title: Partner choice, relationship satisfaction, and oral contraception: The congruency hypothesis.

decisions.quote: Contrary to previous studies' findings, no main effects of HC congruency status were detected for any of the dependent variables (Fig. 1), and effect sizes were invariably close to zero (Table 1). Despite using exactly the same measures as used in all previous studies except one (Russell et al., 2014) as well as additional, well-validated alternative measures, we were unable to confirm the results concerning sexual satisfaction reported by Roberts, Little, et al. (2014) and Russell et al. (2014), or the results concerning jealousy reported by Cobey et al. (2013).
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists at the supplied context paths. In a new sample of N = 948 Finnish women using the exact relationship and sexual satisfaction items from Roberts, Little, et al. (2014) alongside validated measures (PRQC and FSFI), the authors empirically retest the association between hormonal contraceptive (HC) congruency and sexual/relationship satisfaction reported by Roberts, S. C., Little, A. C., Burriss, R. P., Cobey, K. D., Klapilová, K., Havlíček, J., et al. (2014), 'Partner choice, relationship satisfaction, and oral contraception: The congruency hypothesis', Psychological Science, 25, 1497-1503 (no DOI printed in source). This original work is distinct from the only shipped row, input_row_index 2414 (10.1016/j.paid.2013.04.031, Cobey, Roberts, & Buunk, 2013, Personality and Individual Differences, 55, 569-573, which tested HC congruency and jealousy in N = 121 women), and from sibling target_index 2 (Russell et al., 2014, PNAS, 111, 17081-17086, a longitudinal study of newlywed wives). Report equivalence does not apply, and Roberts, Little, et al. (2014) is genuinely absent from the shipped pairs.
